parsed.attack: Centriq did exactly this and shut down on 31 January 2026: photograph the nameplate, get the equipment identified with the parts that fit it, keep a dated record you can hand on. It had a curated parts database behind the recognition that an on-device model does not have, and it still could not survive the interval between a record being written and a pressure tank actually failing, which is measured in years rather than weeks. The shareable-artefact loop is the same one Centriq ran - records passed to contractors and buyers - and this idea's own third kill criterion, 5% opened by a second person within 90 days, is set at a level that concedes the loop barely turns.
parsed.strongest_defence: One-time pricing means the product never has to be re-justified at a renewal, which is the specific thing that killed the subscription version, and a rural well-and-septic house has an enforced annual cadence - water testing, pump servicing, septic pumping - that a suburban homeowner does not.
parsed.verdict_reason: Charging once genuinely dissolves the renewal half of Centriq's cause, but the years-long gap between capture and need, and the missing verified parts mapping, are untouched.
